newsitem.title: New Zealand: NZ long end rallies at close on U.S. strength.
newsitem.headline: NZ long end rallies at close on U.S. strength.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against yesterday's close
* NZ long end manages to rally at close, rest of curve flat
* RBNZ's economic projections next Thursday awaited
The long end of New Zealand's yield curve managed a small rally at Thursday's close in response to offshore strength, but the rest of the market closed largely unchanged.

The 11/06 maturity rallied four basis points to 7.71 percent as U.S. Treasuries took a liking to the latest Humphrey Hawkins testimony from Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan. The New York market got quite bullish as Greenspan's comments eased fears of rising interest rates.
Local bond dealers said volumes had been extremely moderate and the short end had struggled.
"The long end is the only one that outperformed, really. There has been some buying in the 06s -- there's been reasonable support in that part of the curve on the day," one said.
A small slip in the currency's Trade-Weighted index to 68.87 from 68.94 did not help sentiment in the money market, where the 90-day bank bill rates closed two basis points higher at 7.70 percent.

The front futures contract shed a point to 92.28, but bill dealers said flows were minimal and the market was basically marking time until the Reserve Bank issued its economic projections on March 13.

The overnight cash rate moved up to 7.50 percent from 7.40 percent at the open, and dealers said it was finally coming into line with the rest of the curve after being held down artificially by market participants wanting to fund assets.
Dealers said U.S. non-farm payrolls data would provide local bonds with some direction until the key RBNZ release next Thursday.

One bond dealer said he expected another reasonably quiet session on Friday. While while there was room for some short covering ahead of the economic projections, the market was too nervous to stage a big rally, he said.
